name: Application should help an artist
request: Application should help an artist to open up an image and: see grey scale  version of  the image with selected number of levels, crop the image, select the number of levels for colored version of image and make the kubelka-munk mixtures for the pallete. The artist should select what kind of paints, acylic/oil or watercolor, for the painting. It should be possible to select which kind of grid would be drawn over the image, rule of third, fibonacci spiral or grid. Artist creates palletes on the begining for instace, watercolor: Crimson PG__, transparent;  Cobalt Blue PB__, half-transparent; Yellow deep PY__, opaque etc. and another pallete watercolor 2., acrylic 1, acrylic 2, etc.

Next I'll check the acrylic and oil wording and the PDF in Glaze mode.I'll add a self-test step that exports the PDF in Glaze mode too.All 29 steps pass. Let me look at the glazing page of the PDF itself.I can't open PDF pages here, so I'll render page 4 to a picture with macOS's built-in PDF support.The PDF looks good. On the cover, two lines still say "mixes" in Glaze mode, so I'll fix them.Both builds are clean and all 29 steps pass. Now the numbers sheet.Now the README, changelog and project notes, as earlier turns did.Now Craft Anything's check, plus an open question to record: how thick a glaze really is.Everything passes. Recording where things stand.Each acrylic and oil paint now has its own glaze thickness. Next I'm making the white ratio clearer: it will read "1 paint + 3 white".Every acrylic and oil paint now runs from "a faint veil" (pale) to "strong" (its full colour), and a veil of black is a light grey. Next: the checkbox label, plus an acrylic check in the self-test.All 30 steps pass. To see acrylic glazing on screen, I'll add a `--medium` option for screenshots.I'll add a test that "strong" and "a veil" mean the same thing for every acrylic and oil paint.The new test is too strict for pale yellows: a yellow glaze barely changes lightness, it gets more saturated. I'll compare the overall colour difference instead.All 23 unit tests pass. Updating the sheet for the final thickness rule.The oil recipes display correctly; greens are only "close" or "rough" because the starter oil palette has no transparent yellow or green. Cleaning up and running the final check.There's now a **Mix / Glaze** switch beside the paints. In Glaze mode each colour becomes a layered recipe, such as "Cobalt Blue, then Crimson, then Lemon Yellow", with the strength of each layer and small swatches showing the colour after each one. Watercolour recipes start with a wash on the paper; acrylic and oil recipes start with one paint mixed with white, or the bare white ground. Up to two glazes of transparent or half-transparent paints go on top, each picture remembers the choice, and the PDF brochure lists the glazing recipes.

It builds, and all 30 steps of the automatic run-through pass, including new glazing checks for watercolour, acrylic and the PDF; I looked at the watercolour, oil and phone layouts on screen. With the starter palettes, glazing usually matches within the "excellent" to "good" range. Greens in the oil palette come out only "close" or "rough", because that palette has no transparent yellow or green. How thick each glaze strength is ("a veil", "thin", "strong" and so on) is my estimate, not measured from real paint, and the first layer is always a single paint rather than a mix.

I also updated the README, the changelog and the project notes outside the app folder, and added two screenshot options for showing Glaze mode and a chosen paint type. Nothing is committed yet. A good next step would be to paint one transparent colour at a few strengths over white and compare it with the swatches in the app, so the glaze strengths can be set from real paint.
